items.title: Telstra returning CEO Vicki Brady 'deeply sorry' for national outage
items.description: Telstra chief executive Vicki Brady apologises to the company's customers, saying the telco let them down and that investigations into the cause of Wednesday's Telstra outage are continuing.

items.title: Iran targets US military sites in Gulf as Israel warns it could 'strike again'
items.description: Iranian armed forces launched reciprocal attacks on US military infrastructure in Gulf states following US strikes on Iran's south and east regions, straining a three-week-old ceasefire.

items.title: Not only is the war not over, it is at a dangerous inflection point
items.description: Not only is the war not over, it is once again at a dangerous inflection point, as the US and Iran revert to military options to deal with differences over their interim peace agreement.

items.title: Trump tariff fight resumes as Australia tells US it has no evidence
items.description: The Australian embassy in Washington lodges an objection to the Trump administration's proposal for a 12.5 per cent tariff on Australian imports.

items.title: X under fire for 'shocking disrespect' of antisemitism royal commission
items.description: Social media giants, including Elon Musk's X Corp, have come under fire with the royal commission on antisemitism expressing frustration at platforms' refusal to engage.

items.title: Live: CBA accused of hiding reasons for hundreds of job cuts
items.description: The nation's biggest bank, CBA, has been accused by the finance union of hiding the reason behind hundreds of job cuts. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: The meteorite at the centre of a 'culture war' between the UK and Australia
items.description: The fight to claim a 3.5-tonne space rock didn't just kickstart a publicity battle that divided an empire — it also left a gaping hole in culture. Centuries on, the question remains: Who owned it?

items.title: Live: Hanson doubles down on call for Coalition to work with One Nation
items.description: Pauline Hanson has doubled down on calls for the Coalition to work with One Nation. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: H5 bird flu strain detected in Australian seabird for first time
items.description: Agriculture Minister Julie Collins says CSIRO lab testing has confirmed the deadly strain in a greater crested tern found in South Australia's Limestone Coast.

items.title: As a pup, authorities saved Neil the seal from drowning. Now, he's here to stay
items.description: Neil the seal has left his resting spot in Tasmania, leaving behind a wildly popular social media catalogue of bollard-bashing, fence-crushing videos.

items.title: Police slide into DMs of underworld group chat with warning
items.description: An encrypted phone network allegedly used by Sydney's underworld to orchestrate murders, kidnappings and drug deals has been infiltrated by NSW Police after they arrested a trio accused of running the "VIP Network".

items.title: Inside the alleged plot to kill Trump and Musk at UFC White House event
items.description: Eight men have been accused of planning a drone and shooting attack that aimed to kill the US president and SpaceX founder at the UFC Freedom 250 event held at the White House in June.

items.title: Quick hits: It's the Mbappé show again, as England defender cops ban
items.description: An England defender pays the price for a terrible red-card tackle, and it's the Mbappé show in Boston as France advances. Here are today's quick hits.

items.title: 'Leave him to me': Man dressed as bin challenges Nigel Farage
items.description: Nigel Farage is facing intensifying scrutiny over his finances and millions of dollars' worth of donations. Here's how he got here.

items.title: These are the best new TV shows of 2026 so far
items.description: A mountain of TV has landed in 2026 and we've sifted through it all to deliver you the ones worth your time (or at least a binge-watch).

items.title: How to choose the right potato for any meal you're cooking
items.description: Potatoes are undeniably versatile and tasty but choosing which variety to buy has never been more complicated. Brushed or washed? Yellow, white or pink? Mashing or roasting? And now there are low-carb spuds too.

items.title: Friday news quiz: Red cards, ballistic missiles and Pam the Bird

items.title: Looking back at Bonnie Tyler's impact on pop culture
items.description: Tyler's music continuously found newer, younger audiences thanks to it soundtracking memorable scenes in movies throughout the decades.

items.title: PM to unveil AI agenda as government seeks to calm copyright concerns
items.description: A draft document, seen by ABC, reveals AI, gambling and the Middle East are expected to feature heavily in Labor's upcoming national conference debate.

items.title: Workers' pay has not kept pace with productivity growth in 30 years
items.description: Research suggests that the typical worker's pay has not kept pace with productivity growth in Australia for 30 years.

items.title: Modi tells Melbourne crowd India aspires to 'grow more, achieve more'
items.description: More than 20,000 people have given a rapturous welcome to Narendra Modi at Melbourne's Docklands Stadium as Anthony Albanese heaps praise on Australia's Indian diaspora.

items.title: How China's military goals in the Pacific are rapidly progressing
items.description: China's firing of a dummy warhead was the first time in two years it tested its long-range missile arsenal — and the first time ever it had launched such a rocket from a nuclear-powered submarine.

items.title: Girls married off as a climate change 'coping strategy'
items.description: Climate change is now believed to be a leading contributor to more frequent and younger nuptials, with 12 million girls tipped to become child brides this year.

items.title: Wildlife carers fronting WA's bird flu response left feeling let down
items.description: WA wildlife carers say the state government has forgotten them as PPE supplies and veterinary resources run dangerously low.

items.title: Cancelled musician loses fight against orchestra over political beliefs
items.description: The unlawful discrimination case brought by Jayson Gillham against the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra sprung from the orchestra's decision to cancel his scheduled performance over comments he made about Gaza.
